continuity.teaching_arc: A curse weakens Indra; the devas petition Vishnu; the churning is planned and begun; the fully tortoise-formed Kurma supports and lifts Mandara; the gods renew their work; Vasuki’s poison brings heat; Vishnu alone resumes churning as the poet closes in prayer.
continuity.narrative_arc: Move from an intimate celestial insult to collective petition, counsel, the ocean churning crisis and resolution; keep each scene as one legible mural moment.
continuity.vishnu_anatomy: In divine narrative form, use the established deep-blue Narayana identity and exactly four naturally attached arms where the scene calls for the four-armed form. In D027 stanza 11 the verse says karayuga: Vishnu has exactly two attached arms, both gripping the same Vasuki. In stanzas 6–7 the avatar is a complete tortoise, not a half-human form. Do not show Krishna/Yashoda.
continuity.brahma_anatomy: When Brahma appears, exactly four heads total with three distinct faces visible from the front and the fourth turned behind; exactly four attached arms.
continuity.vasuki_contract: One continuous serpent body and one head; asuras hold the head end and devas hold the tail end in the churning scenes. Do not use Adishesha’s couch/canopy contract.
continuity.crowd_anatomy: Devas and asuras are distinct natural two-armed, two-legged humanoids. Keep groups small and visually varied; no cloned repeated faces or fused bodies.
continuity.style: Fresh flat matte mineral mural with firm dark contours, broad earthy color fields, shallow decorative space and restrained ornament. D001 S004 and S008 are rendering references only; the approved Guruvayurappan and Brahma sheets guide identity/iconography only.
continuity.bhattathiri: Only appears in S011 because the supplied closing caption names the poet; use the exact older clean-shaven identity candidate as an identity cue only. No beard or moustache; not an approved master.
